But this record is a correction notice that does nothing except re-date the award: it states no scope, no deliverable and no appropriation, so there is no evidence that the $625,000,000 IDIQ funds the development line rather than BLI FBLOST 'Family of Beyond Line-of-Sight Terminals', the procurement line for the same terminal family. A program name with no work described does not meet §1.

proposals.program_name: The F-15 Eagle Passive Active Warning Survivability System (EPAWSS)
proposals.lexicon_quote: The F-15 Eagle Passive Active Warning Survivability System (EPAWSS)
proposals.announcement_evidence: the F-15 Eagle Passive Active Warning Survivability System full rate production
proposals.rationale: The announcement carries the index row's name almost letter for letter, and the row it matches is BLI F15EWS 'F-15 EPAW' in the aircraft procurement book (doc 407) - the right appropriation for a full-rate production award obligating fiscal 2023, 2024 and 2025 procurement funds. Two other rows carry EPAWSS variants, PE 0207171F (RDT&E, excluded by the procurement funding) and BLI F015EX 'F-15EX' (excluded because this buys Group A and Group B retrofit kits with interim contractor support, not new F-15EX aircraft); the F15EWS row is also the only one whose name begins with the 'F-15' the announcement uses.

refute_a.reason: Fiscal 2023, 2024 and 2025 procurement funds are obligated and BLI F15EWS sits in doc 407, the aircraft procurement book, so a full-rate-production award matches the line's appropriation; the Group A and Group B kits are EPAWSS itself - the F-15 is the platform, the line is the EPAWSS modification line - and the interim contractor support lay-in material is a minor rider on a procurement action.

refute_b.reason: REFUTED: three index rows own an EPAWSS name - F15EWS and F015EX (both doc 407, so the procurement funding cannot separate them) plus 0207171F - and F015EX's name "Eagle Passive Active Warning Survivability System (EPAWSS)" is the announcement's string minus the F-15 prefix, so the leading "F-15" is too thin a discriminator between two procurement lines in the same book.

proposals.announcement_evidence: the production of the Wideband Global Satellite Communication Space Vehicle 11
proposals.rationale: 'Wideband Global Satellite Communication' is the spelled-out form of the SATCOM abbreviation in the index row under BLI GAP000 'Wideband Gapfiller Satellites(Space)', the space procurement line that buys WGS satellites - and the announcement obligates $300,000,000 of fiscal 2018 procurement funds to produce a specific space vehicle, which is that line's own product. PE 1206433SF mentions WGS-11 and WGS-12 in its narrative, but it is the RDT&E element covering WGS modernization efforts such as BOOM, GSCCE and MAJE; satellite production hardware belongs to the procurement line, so the appropriation named in the announcement resolves the two.

refute_a.reason: Fiscal 2018 procurement funds of $300,000,000 are obligated and BLI GAP000 sits in doc 416, the space procurement book, so producing Wideband Global SATCOM Space Vehicle 11 is the line's own hardware buy; the satellite is the program's product rather than a platform the contract supports, and 'Wideband Gapfiller Satellites(Space)' is the WGS procurement line, not an aggregate.

refute_b.reason: REFUTED: the announcement names Space Vehicle 11, and the index carries "WGS-11" as a name owned by a DIFFERENT PE (1206433SF, doc 417) - a more specific match than GAP000's generic "The Wideband Global SATCOM (WGS)" - so the index itself assigns this space vehicle's name elsewhere.
